To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HIV-1 accessory Vpr protein potentiates glucorticoid (GC) induction of receptor of activated nuclear factor-κB ligands (RANKL).
HIV-1 accessory gene product Vpr enhances production and activity of receptor of activated nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANL) through potentiation of glucocoicoid receptor (GR) activity.
Vpr enhances RANKL production through a GC receptor-dependent, G2 cell cycle-independent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of Vpr action.
a new mechanism of action for the HIV-1 accessory factor Vpr that may contribute to the pathogenesis of HIV infection.
the role of the HIV-1 Vpr protein in regulation of cytokine expression and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV-1 Vpr potentiately enhances production of receptor activator of NF-κB (RANKL), a key cytokine in osteoclastogenesis, via potentiation of the activity of the glucocorticoid hormone receptor.
Vpr is a novel positive regulator of GC-induced expression of RANKL.
HIV-1 Vpr is a novel positive regulator of RANKL production in T cells and that this effect is dependent on the GC receptor and independent of the cell cycle arrest function of Vpr.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Vpr enhances production RANKL, a cytokine that is critical to osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption, through a GC receptor-dependent mechanism.
HIV-1 Vpr is a potent enhancer of GC-induced transcription, and we have identified a novel mechanism of this effect.

The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-1 Vpr can potentiate GC-induced transcription of RANKL.
